entries.title: Jeremiah 34:1
segments:
vv 1-7. 
 
They who persist in acting contrary to God's declared will, involve themselves in irremediable ruin.

entries.title: Jeremiah 34:5
segments: From a comparison of this verse with

, it appears that Zedekiah, though never restored to his throne, was after some time released from close confinement, and treated with the honor due to his former dignity.  The same was true of Jehoiachin.

entries.title: Jeremiah 34:7
segments: Lachish--Azekah; cities in the plain country of Judah, south-west of Jerusalem.

entries.title: Jeremiah 34:8
segments: To proclaim liberty unto them; that is, to the Hebrew man-servants and maid-servants, in compliance with the law of Moses.
This proclamaiton seems to have been made under the pressure of the siege.  But afterwards, when the Chaldean army had temporarily departed from Jerusalem,
, the princes and people again reduced to bondage their servants whom they had set free.

entries.title: Jeremiah 34:11
segments: Those acts of duty upon which men enter unwillingly, under the influence of fear, are generally abandoned as soon as the outward pressure is removed.

entries.title: Jeremiah 34:13
segments:
vv 13-14. 
 
By the law of Moses the Hebrews were forbidden to oppress their brethren, and reduce them to perpetual bondage.  The Christian religion has abolished the distinction between Jews and Gentiles.  It teaches us to regard all men as brethren,

entries.title: Jeremiah 34:15
segments:
vv 15-22. 
 
Perfidy in our dealings with men is a heinous sin, which God will punish; but its guilt is greatly aggravated when they whom we deceive by false promises are weak and unable to defend themselves.  Of all such God is the protector and avenger.

entries.title: Jeremiah 34:16
segments: Polluted my name; by violating their covenant made before God in his house; an act of shameless perjury.
